description: Rules compiled for source profile multisource-full-http.

normalization_contract.url_decode: percent-decode without converting plus to space

sources.name: OWASP ModSecurity Core Rule Set
sources.scope_note: Generic HTTP attack classes adapted for the normalized field model, including capability-gated request, upload, multipart and response variants. Not a drop-in CRS replacement.

sources.name: SigmaHQ main rule repository
sources.scope_note: Webserver signatures only. Author attribution is retained on every derived rule and must also appear in alert output.

sources.name: Google Cloud security analytics
sources.scope_note: HTTP load-balancer detections that can be expressed using the Cloudflare event contract.

sources.name: Google SecOps community detection rules
sources.scope_note: Community YARA-L rules with directly mappable inbound HTTP fields.

sources.name: MITRE Cyber Analytics Repository
sources.scope_note: No CAR analytic is directly an HTTP attack signature. CAR-2021-01-001 contributes the distinct-target scanning model adapted here to URI enumeration.

sources.name: Splunk Security Content
sources.scope_note: HTTP behavior mapped from Splunk Web detections, including URI rules and locally refined payload conjunctions. Endpoint-only, alert-only and outbound context is not fabricated.

sources.name: Elastic Security detection rules
sources.scope_note: cPanel/WHM and React2Shell variants are retained with required HTTP capabilities and Elastic-2.0 provenance. Endpoint and packet context unavailable in normalized HTTP remains excluded.

sources.name: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
sources.scope_note: Guidance adapted into locally authored candidate heuristics for uploads, XML/JSON, GraphQL and JWT. Thresholds are local policy choices, not upstream executable detection rules.

rules.title: Cloudflare security control acted on request
rules.description: Surfaces a request on which a Cloudflare security control took a non-allow action.
false_positives: Expected policy enforcement and explicitly configured logging actions.
rules.tuning: Treat this as high-confidence telemetry, not proof that exploitation succeeded. Suppress known policy-only rule IDs if necessary.

rules.title: Cloudflare WAF attack score indicates likely attack
rules.description: Detects low Cloudflare attack scores, where lower non-zero values represent higher attack likelihood.
false_positives: Benign requests misclassified by managed detection models.
rules.tuning: Keep the non-zero guard because zero can mean not scored. Adjust the maximum only after measuring local precision.

rules.title: Known web scanner user agent
rules.description: Detects default user agents from common web reconnaissance and exploitation tools.
false_positives: Authorized vulnerability scanning and penetration tests.
rules.tuning: Allowlist scanner egress addresses rather than removing tool tokens.

rules.title: Risky or uncommon HTTP method
rules.description: Detects methods commonly disabled on public applications or associated with proxy tunneling and debugging.
false_positives: Legitimate forward proxy CONNECT traffic or deliberate TRACE diagnostics.
rules.tuning: Enable per host; CONNECT is usually invalid for an origin-facing application.

rules.title: HTTP method override parameter
rules.description: Detects an attempt to override the request method through a query parameter.
false_positives: Frameworks that intentionally use method override parameters.
rules.tuning: Allowlist only the routes where method override is an intended feature.

rules.title: HTTP request smuggling header conflict
rules.description: Detects simultaneous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers or multiple conflicting transfer encodings.
false_positives: Intermediaries that preserve both headers after safely normalizing the request.
rules.tuning: This rule depends on requestheaders retention; keep exact raw header multiplicity if the ingest format can represent it.

rules.title: CRLF or HTTP header injection in URI
rules.description: Detects encoded carriage-return or newline sequences followed by a header-like token.
false_positives: Applications intentionally accepting encoded multiline content in a query value.
rules.tuning: Do not URL-decode before this match; it intentionally detects encoded CR/LF bytes.

rules.title: Multiple encoding or null-byte evasion
rules.description: Detects double-encoded traversal/metacharacters, overlong UTF-8 traversal forms, and encoded null bytes.
false_positives: Applications transporting already URL-encoded data as a value.
rules.tuning: Prefer endpoint exclusions to globally weakening this evasion signal.

rules.title: Path traversal attempt
rules.description: Detects literal, encoded, double-encoded, slash-reversed, and overlong-UTF traversal sequences.
false_positives: Documentation, security training, or search endpoints containing traversal examples.
rules.tuning: Suppress known content routes; do not exclude based only on 404 because unsuccessful exploit attempts remain useful.

rules.title: Sensitive local file or development artifact probe
rules.description: Detects requests for operating-system credentials, repository metadata, environment files, backup files, and AI coding-assistant artifacts.
false_positives: Public documentation or intentionally served archive files.
rules.tuning: Split by asset type if different response teams own source exposure and OS-file probing.

rules.title: Remote file inclusion attempt
rules.description: Detects URL-valued parameters commonly used to load remote code or templates.
false_positives: Legitimate URL import, webhook, preview, or fetch features.
rules.tuning: Restrict this rule to endpoints that should never fetch a remote resource, or maintain an allowlist of destination hosts.

rules.title: Cloud instance metadata SSRF probe
rules.description: Detects cloud metadata endpoints embedded in a request URI.
false_positives: Security documentation or test payloads submitted through an application.
rules.tuning: Any match on a fetch-capable endpoint should be investigated urgently.

rules.title: Unix command injection payload
rules.description: Detects shell separators or substitutions followed by high-signal system commands.
false_positives: Developer tools or search interfaces receiving shell syntax as content.
rules.tuning: Body content is absent from the target log schema, so this covers URI and query payloads only.

rules.title: Shellshock exploit payload
rules.description: Detects the Shellshock function prefix followed by shell metacharacters in URI, user agent, referer, or request header values.
false_positives: Security testing payloads.
rules.tuning: This is a high-confidence legacy exploit signature; alert even when the response is 4xx.

rules.title: Windows command or webshell payload in URI
rules.description: Detects common Windows discovery and execution commands passed as request parameters.
false_positives: Wiki, documentation, or search routes containing command examples.
rules.tuning: Exclude content/search routes rather than broad command names.

rules.title: PHP code or wrapper injection
rules.description: Detects PHP tags, dangerous stream wrappers, serialized objects, and high-risk function calls in the URI.
false_positives: Programming documentation or code-search applications.
rules.tuning: Route exclusions are safer than deleting individual dangerous function names.

rules.title: Node.js prototype pollution or code injection
rules.description: Detects prototype-chain keys and common Node.js process execution constructs in request parameters.
false_positives: JavaScript documentation, package registries, and source browsers.
rules.tuning: Raise confidence when keys occur as parameter names rather than free text.

rules.title: LDAP injection expression
rules.description: Detects encoded or literal LDAP filter operators combined with common identity attributes.
false_positives: Applications that intentionally expose LDAP-filter syntax.
rules.tuning: Promote to production after validating URI encoding against local traffic.

rules.title: SQL injection payload
rules.description: Combines high-signal SQL union, boolean, timing, metadata, comment, and command-execution patterns into one canonical alert.
false_positives: Search, documentation, observability, and code-hosting routes containing SQL text.
rules.tuning: Do not exclude 404 responses globally; use route-aware suppression and score native WAF corroboration higher.

rules.title: Cross-site scripting payload
rules.description: Detects scriptable tags, event handlers, JavaScript URIs, and browser object access after bounded canonicalization.
false_positives: Web development, documentation, WYSIWYG editor, and code-search routes.
rules.tuning: Use endpoint-aware exclusions. The transform order is security-relevant and must be bounded to two URL decodes.

rules.title: Server-side template injection payload
rules.description: Detects common Jinja, Twig, Freemarker, Java EL, ERB, and Spring expression syntax in URI values.
false_positives: Template playgrounds, documentation, and source-code search.
rules.tuning: Escalate matches that contain both expression delimiters and a dangerous object or class token.

rules.title: Java serialized object or gadget payload
rules.description: Detects Java serialization magic bytes and common gadget or runtime execution tokens in an HTTP URI.
false_positives: Java development documentation or artifact inspection endpoints.
rules.tuning: The schema does not include request bodies, so serialized POST bodies are out of scope unless separately ingested.

rules.title: Log4Shell JNDI lookup
rules.description: Detects literal or URL-encoded JNDI lookup expressions in URI, user agent, referer, or request header values.
false_positives: Security scanners, honeypots, and content that intentionally stores exploit strings.
rules.tuning: Preserve header values in requestheaders; attackers commonly place this payload outside the URI.

rules.title: JNDI exploit kit endpoint
rules.description: Detects distinctive JNDI-Exploit-Kit payload-serving endpoints.
false_positives: Research systems intentionally mirroring exploit-kit paths.
rules.tuning: This is a narrow, high-confidence path signature and should rarely need tuning.

rules.title: ReGeorg webshell protocol
rules.description: Detects ReGeorg command parameters combined with POST and absent user-agent and referer values.
false_positives: Applications using the same generic command parameter vocabulary.
rules.tuning: If empty values are normalized to null at ingest, the rule already handles both representations.

rules.title: F5 BIG-IP iControl bash endpoint request
rules.description: Detects POST requests to the F5 iControl REST utility bash endpoint.
false_positives: Legitimate F5 administration through this endpoint.
rules.tuning: Limit legitimate administration to trusted source addresses, then alert on all other matches.

rules.title: Spring4Shell exploit parameters
rules.description: Detects the class-loader property chain and JSP command parameter patterns used in Spring4Shell probes.
false_positives: Requests carrying Java property names as documentation or test content.
rules.tuning: The upstream detection explicitly covers URL/query variants only; request-body-only exploitation remains invisible.

rules.title: SharePoint ToolPane exploitation chain
rules.description: Detects the POST path, query parameters, and signout referrer associated with CVE-2025-49706 exploitation.
false_positives: Rare legitimate administrative use of the exact ToolPane chain.
rules.tuning: Keep all four request constraints together to preserve the upstream rule's precision.

rules.title: Successful IIS shortname enumeration probe
rules.description: Detects successful IIS tilde shortname fuzzing requests.
false_positives: Legitimate legacy IIS paths containing tilde aliases.
rules.tuning: Only enable on IIS-backed applications; this preserves the upstream success-status requirement.

rules.title: Adobe ColdFusion arbitrary file read endpoint
rules.description: Detects successful POST requests to the ColdFusion CKEditor path used by CVE-2023-26360 probes.
false_positives: Legitimate ColdFusion CKEditor requests to the same legacy route.
rules.tuning: Restrict to hosts that run ColdFusion; retain the success status to match the upstream detection.

rules.title: Confluence pre-auth OGNL injection endpoint
rules.description: Detects successful POST requests to the Confluence Velocity template endpoint used by CVE-2023-22527.
false_positives: Legitimate Confluence requests to the template endpoint.
rules.tuning: Enable only for Confluence assets. Body-level OGNL confirmation is unavailable in the Cloudflare schema.

rules.title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect SetupWizard authentication bypass
rules.description: Detects successful POST requests to alternate SetupWizard paths used for ScreenConnect authentication bypass.
false_positives: Legitimate initial ScreenConnect setup activity.
rules.tuning: Any SetupWizard access after initial deployment is suspicious; restrict by ScreenConnect host.

rules.title: Ivanti Connect Secure command injection chain
rules.description: Detects successful requests to traversal-based Ivanti API paths associated with authentication bypass and command injection.
false_positives: Authorized vulnerability scans against an Ivanti appliance.
rules.tuning: Restrict to Ivanti hosts and allowlist approved scanner sources.

rules.title: Jenkins CLI arbitrary file read request
rules.description: Detects a successful POST to the Jenkins CLI remoting endpoint used by CVE-2024-23897.
false_positives: Legitimate Jenkins CLI remoting-disabled sessions.
rules.tuning: Restrict to Jenkins hosts and correlate with unusual CLI use or exposed-controller access.

rules.title: WordPress Bricks Builder render endpoint RCE attempt
rules.description: Detects a successful POST to the Bricks Builder render endpoint used by CVE-2024-25600.
false_positives: Legitimate Bricks Builder rendering requests.
rules.tuning: This is route-level detection because request bodies are unavailable; correlate with WAF RCE score and restrict to vulnerable plugin assets.

rules.title: Tomcat session deserialization trigger
rules.description: Detects the dotted JSESSIONID and server error combination used to trigger a previously uploaded malicious Tomcat session.
false_positives: A legitimate application using dotted JSESSIONID values and returning 500.
rules.tuning: Enable on Tomcat assets and correlate with a prior PUT request that uploaded a session file.

rules.title: Fortinet administrative API authentication bypass path
rules.description: Detects access to the Fortinet system administrator API associated with CVE-2022-40684.
false_positives: Legitimate Fortinet administrator API use, especially GET inventory requests.
rules.tuning: Restrict to Fortinet management hosts and trusted administrator source ranges; consider requiring PUT for higher precision.

rules.title: cPanel WHM CRLF authentication bypass response shape
rules.description: Detects GET-root requests with Basic authorization that receive a redirect to a newly minted cPanel session path.
false_positives: Authorized vulnerability scanners reproducing the exploit shape.
rules.tuning: Cloudflare lacks destination port, so enable only for hostnames serving cPanel or WHM. Exact raw duplicate headers and decoded Basic content are not available.

rules.title: Repeated failed login requests from one client
rules.description: Detects a burst of denied requests to common authentication endpoints from one client IP.
false_positives: Shared NATs, broken clients, load tests, and password-manager retries.
rules.tuning: Tune paths and threshold per application; use a user or account dimension if separately available.

rules.title: High-cardinality path enumeration
rules.description: Detects a client probing many distinct paths with many unsuccessful responses.
false_positives: Search crawlers, cache warmers, uptime fleets, and front-end asset bursts.
rules.tuning: Exclude verified bots and known internal scanners; tune thresholds by host traffic profile.

rules.title: Repeated sensitive-path discovery sweep
rules.description: Detects one client probing multiple distinct administrative, repository, secret, and framework paths.
false_positives: Authorized scanners and security monitoring.
rules.tuning: Add application-specific sensitive paths and allowlist scanner IP ranges.

rules.title: Single-client request burst
rules.description: Detects a high request count from one client over one minute.
false_positives: Large NATs, API clients, crawlers, load tests, and traffic spikes.
rules.tuning: This is a baseline starting point, not a universal threshold. Segment by host and known client class.

rules.title: Distributed identical malicious payload campaign
rules.description: Detects the same suspicious URI being requested by many distinct source IPs in a short window.
false_positives: Coordinated security scans and widespread benign clients requesting a missing common asset.
rules.tuning: Hash or truncate the grouping URI after stable canonicalization to bound memory and prevent attacker-controlled cardinality.

rules.title: SQL injection payload in request body
rules.description: Detects high-signal SQL union, boolean, timing, metadata, and command-execution patterns in a decoded request body.
false_positives: APIs intentionally accepting SQL, query builders, or code snippets.
rules.tuning: Apply content-type and route-aware suppression. Enforce body size and decompression limits before evaluation.

rules.title: Cross-site scripting payload in request body
rules.description: Detects scriptable tags, event handlers, JavaScript URIs, and browser object access in decoded form or JSON bodies.
false_positives: WYSIWYG editors, HTML form builders, and APIs designed to accept markup.
rules.tuning: Restrict exclusions to known rich-content fields rather than the entire endpoint.

rules.title: Server-side template injection in request body
rules.description: Detects Jinja, Twig, Freemarker, Java EL, ERB, and dangerous template object access in decoded request bodies.
false_positives: Template editors, CI configuration APIs, and developer playgrounds.
rules.tuning: Score dangerous object tokens more highly than delimiter-only matches.

rules.title: Command injection payload in request body
rules.description: Detects shell separators or substitutions followed by high-signal system commands in request bodies.
false_positives: Build APIs, shell consoles, and developer automation endpoints.
rules.tuning: Restrict body retention and alert excerpts to the smallest evidence span.

rules.title: Java serialized object in request body
rules.description: Detects binary or Base64 Java serialization magic and common gadget-chain markers in request bodies.
false_positives: Java serialization gateways and security research systems.
rules.tuning: Preserve binary bodies losslessly or expose a Base64 representation with an explicit adapter contract.

rules.title: Log4Shell JNDI lookup in request body
rules.description: Detects literal or encoded JNDI lookup expressions in request bodies.
false_positives: Security scanners and systems intentionally storing exploit strings.
rules.tuning: Apply to textual and structured bodies after bounded decompression.

rules.title: Spring4Shell class-loader payload in request body
rules.description: Detects the Spring class-loader property chain and JSP webshell configuration in POST form data.
false_positives: Security tests and unusual Java configuration-management APIs.
rules.tuning: Require the full property-chain prefix; do not reduce this to generic class.module tokens.

rules.title: React Server Components RCE payload
rules.description: Detects React Flight reference structure combined with prototype-pollution keys in a POST body.
false_positives: Security scanners reproducing the exploit structure.
rules.tuning: The upstream rule also uses response-body evidence. This request-only variant is therefore test status.

rules.title: Duplicate raw HTTP request header
rules.description: Detects repeated request header field names before an intermediary collapses them into a map.
false_positives: Headers whose grammar legitimately permits repeated instances and adapters that split comma lists incorrectly.
rules.tuning: Preserve original header instances and ordering. Repeated Accept-Encoding and Connection alone are ignored because RFC 9110 sections 5.2, 7.6.1, and 12.5.3 permit combining their list-valued fields. This does not validate their values or HTTP-version legality. Host, Content-Length, and Transfer-Encoding duplicates still alert. Other list-valued headers can still produce noise; expand exemptions only after protocol review.

rules.title: Database error, stack trace, or source information leakage
rules.description: Detects database engine errors and Java, PHP, ASP.NET, or IIS diagnostic details exposed in a response body.

match.value: (?:you have an error in your sql syntax|warning: mysql_|pg_query\(|postgresql.*error|ora-[0-9]{5}|sqlstate\[[0-9a-z]+\]|exception in thread \x22|at [a-z0-9_.$]+\([a-z0-9_]+\.java:[0-9]+\)|fatal error:|stack trace:|server error in '/[^']*' application|system\.(?:web|io)\.[a-z]+exception)

false_positives: Developer documentation and observability interfaces intentionally displaying errors.
rules.tuning: Sample and redact response evidence; never persist full responses solely for alerting.

rules.title: Server-side script filename in file upload
rules.description: Flags executable upload extensions, including trailing-dot and null/semicolon variants. Filename evidence alone does not establish execution.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Allow authorized code/package upload routes. Evaluate decoded client filenames before basename stripping.

rules.title: Traversal components in uploaded filename
rules.description: Flags parent-directory components in upload filenames before path sanitization.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Preserve path separators in the adapter; a basename-only field cannot support this rule.

rules.title: Server configuration filename in file upload
rules.description: Flags uploads named for web-server or per-directory interpreter configuration, which can alter how nearby files execute.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Restrict to file-upload endpoints that do not intentionally accept application deployment bundles.

rules.title: PHP session filename upload attempt
rules.description: Identifies upload names shaped like PHP session storage, including the SessionReaper attack class. A matching filename does not identify a vulnerable product.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Correlate with application identity and the upload destination before attributing CVE-2025-54236.

rules.title: PHP execution primitive inside an uploaded file
rules.description: Requires a PHP opening tag and a nearby execution call in the same decoded file part. It is a candidate uploaded webshell signal.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Source-code repositories and developer uploads are common benign matches. Content beyond the bounded proximity is not covered.

rules.title: Content-Transfer-Encoding in a multipart form part
rules.description: Flags a deprecated transfer-encoding header inside an actual multipart form part; body text resembling a header is insufficient.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Legacy upload clients can use this header legitimately. Treat as a parser-evasion candidate.

rules.title: Multipart charset outside the supported text encodings
rules.description: Flags UTF-7/16/32 declarations in parsed part Content-Type or global _charset_ values that can produce differing decoder views.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: This is a selected encoding policy, not the full CRS MIME grammar or a complete charset allowlist.

rules.title: Web directory index returned in response
rules.description: Detects common Apache/nginx-style index pages or IIS parent-directory markers in returned HTML.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Public mirrors deliberately publish indexes. Use route policy and response status to prioritize.

rules.title: CGI interpreter source returned in response
rules.description: Detects a response beginning with a recognizable script interpreter line, consistent with source being served instead of executed.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Script download portals and source viewers are legitimate. Restrict by route and content disposition.

rules.title: PHP source returned in response
rules.description: Requires both a PHP open tag and a PHP-specific variable or function in the response, reducing keyword-only alerts.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Developer documentation and intentional source exports can match; no HTML-entity decoding is applied.

rules.title: Sensitive Ruby template expression returned in response
rules.description: Flags unrendered ERB expressions that reference environment secrets, Rails credentials, or local files.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Intentional Ruby source examples are benign; this covers selected ERB constructs rather than all template leakage.

rules.title: GraphQL schema introspection request
rules.description: Identifies schema-discovery fields from a parsed GraphQL operation. __typename alone, comments, aliases, and string literals do not qualify.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Introspection is normal for developer tools and public APIs. Enable only where route policy makes it noteworthy.

rules.title: GraphQL depth or alias-count threshold exceeded
rules.description: Flags parsed operation depth above 20 or more than 100 aliases. These are locally chosen candidate thresholds, not universal attack boundaries.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Tune for the schema. Count selected operations with fragments expanded and cycles rejected; this is not resolver cost analysis.

rules.title: Large GraphQL operation batch
rules.description: Flags a parsed HTTP GraphQL batch containing more than 10 operation requests. Ordinary JSON arrays are not GraphQL batches.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: The threshold is locally selected. Tune batching policy and account for legitimate SDK batching.

rules.title: JWT using the unsecured none algorithm
rules.description: Flags the unsecured JOSE algorithm in a structurally parsed compact JWT header. This does not establish that the application accepted it.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Unsigned JWTs may be intentional in a protected protocol. Match only the token presented for authentication.

rules.title: Traversal sequence in JWT verification key identifier
rules.description: Flags path traversal components in the decoded JOSE kid header that could reach a filesystem key lookup.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Do not URL-decode kid unless the application does. A suspicious key identifier does not prove signature verification was bypassed.

rules.title: Prototype-chain keys in parsed JSON request
rules.description: Flags prototype-chain property paths in parsed JSON keys, including escaped keys after JSON decoding; quoted descriptions are excluded.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Only keys count. Trusted schema editors can contain these keys. The adapter must retain every object path before unsafe object merging.

rules.title: NoSQL operator submitted to an authentication endpoint
rules.description: Requires an authentication route and parsed JSON query-operator keys, consistent with a NoSQL login bypass attempt.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Adjust route patterns and accepted JSON schema. Database administration or custom query APIs can legitimately accept these keys.

rules.title: Cloud metadata URL in request body
rules.description: Flags explicit cloud-metadata URLs in a decoded request body, extending the URI-only metadata family.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Configuration uploads and security documentation can contain these URLs. Coverage excludes DNS rebinding and nonstandard numeric IP representations.

rules.title: External XML entity or DTD declaration in request body
rules.description: Flags external file or network identifiers in XML ENTITY/DOCTYPE declarations. It observes syntax without resolving entities.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Legacy XML formats use external DTDs. Comments and embedded examples can match; no entity-expansion or exploit-success claim is made.

rules.title: Apache Commons Text dangerous lookup in request body
rules.description: Adapts the Text4Shell lookup concept to bounded body expressions with script, URL, or DNS lookup syntax.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: Application configuration may intentionally use lookups. The local conjunction replaces the upstream broad keyword score.

rules.title: Confluence text template request with OGNL execution tokens
rules.description: Requires the Confluence template endpoint, POST, and an OGNL/Java execution token in the body. It retains failed attempts without a response-status requirement.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: An adaptation with stronger payload evidence than the upstream endpoint/status query; scope to Confluence assets.

rules.title: Ivanti EPM RecordGoodApp SQL command execution attempt
rules.description: Requires the EPM SOAP endpoint, POST, RecordGoodApp, and xp_cmdshell body evidence, consistent with the CVE-2024-29824 exploit path.
false_positives: Authorized testing or application-specific use; validate against the endpoint's intended behavior.
rules.tuning: No success/status assumption is made. SOAP/XML obfuscation beyond entity decoding requires a richer parser.
